question_text: What is the main difference between a stock dividend and bond coupon?
reference_answer: A dividend is a discretionary equity distribution; a coupon is an issuer debt payment under bond terms.
rubric: Distinguish equity versus contractual debt cash flows

question_text: Why does a firm with positive net income not necessarily have positive cash at year-end?
reference_answer: Accrual net income differs from cash changes; investing and financing activities, plus working capital, alter cash.
rubric: Distinguish net income from net cash change

question_text: A company changes from 100m to 200m shares solely due to a two-for-one stock split. Does the split alone double equity market capitalization?
reference_answer: No. Price per share ordinarily adjusts inversely, so split alone does not create additional total equity value.

question_text: An investor claims a 20% ROE always means a company is operationally better than one with 12% ROE. Identify two counterexamples.
reference_answer: Heavy leverage or a very small equity base can inflate ROE; inconsistent accounting or one-off earnings can also distort comparison.
rubric: Leverage / small equity and nonrecurring profit risks

question_text: In Apple FY2024, approximately how much was R&D expense, in USD billions?
Microsoft FY2024 net income was $88,136m and operating income was $109,433m. Are these the same measure, and what does the gap imply?
reference_answer: Different levels: net income includes nonoperating items and tax effects; operating income excludes those. Difference alone does not identify a specific cause.
rubric: Different income measures; no invented attribution

question_text: Walmart FY2025 inventory was $56,435m versus $54,892m in FY2024. Can you say inventory fell?
Costco FY2024 revenue includes merchandise sales and membership fees. Why can neither revenue category alone be interpreted as segment net income?
reference_answer: Revenue is before relevant costs and allocations; audited segment expense/profit disclosures would be needed.

question_text: Hypothetical: a company has $240m revenue and $60m gross profit. What is gross margin?
Hypothetical: a bond bought for $950 has face value $1,000 and a $40 annual coupon. What is the current yield to two decimals?
Hypothetical: annual net income is $90m and diluted weighted-average shares are 30m. What is diluted EPS?
Hypothetical: operating cash flow is $85m, capex $24m and business acquisitions use $30m. Compute simple CFO-minus-capex FCF and state whether acquisition cash is subtracted in this defined measure.
reference_answer: $61m; acquisitions are not subtracted by the specified simple FCF definition.

question_text: Did Apple FY2024 revenue exceed Microsoft FY2024 revenue in USD millions?
reference_answer: Yes: Apple $391,035m versus Microsoft $245,122m; different fiscal year-ends.

question_text: AMD FY2024 gross profit was $12,725m on $25,785m revenue. NVIDIA FY2025 was $97,858m on $130,497m. Who has a higher reported gross margin?
reference_answer: NVIDIA ~74.99%; AMD ~49.35%; NVIDIA higher on these disclosed periods.
source_ref: AMD:FY2024 gross profit|FY2024 revenue;NVDA:FY2025 gross profit|FY2025 revenue

question_text: P&G FY2024 cash from operations was $19,846m and Costco FY2024 was $11,339m. Is the higher absolute CFO enough to say P&G is more efficient?
reference_answer: No; differences in company scale and capital intensity require denominator/return comparisons.
rubric: Do not equate size to efficiency
source_ref: PG:FY2024 operating cash flow;COST:FY2024 operating cash flow

question_text: AMD FY2024 inventories rose while revenue grew. Explain two plausible reasons and why inventory growth alone does not establish weaker financial health than another semiconductor firm.
reference_answer: Inventory could rise for demand builds or slower turnover; evaluate sales mix, write-downs, inventory days and procurement context before judging.
rubric: Two plausible reasons and evidence limits

question_text: Can a company's historical 10-year share-price increase guarantee its next-year performance?
reference_answer: No; future share returns are uncertain and past performance is not a guaranteed floor.

question_text: A worker must pay rent next month but has invested the entire rent amount in a stock fund. Name the core risk mismatch.
reference_answer: Short-term fixed cash need conflicts with volatile market value; being able to sell does not fix sale price.

question_text: AMD disclosed export and manufacturing risks. Why does one year of revenue growth not negate either risk?
reference_answer: Historical success does not remove future policy/supply shocks; risk is about contingent outcomes.

question_text: An investor says: "An asset can never fall more than 10% because it has never done so in my five-year sample." Identify the statistical error.
reference_answer: A limited past sample does not bound future outcomes; tail events, changing regimes and model uncertainty are omitted.
